source.title: Neurocomputational account of how the human brain decides when to have a break
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA

confidence_rationale: Directly supplies the SMALLEST COMPUTATIONAL FORM of a fatigue/stop-recover signal: a scalar 'cost evidence' that accumulates during effort and dissipates during rest, with an UPPER bound triggering stop and a LOWER bound triggering resume -- a hysteretic two-bound accumulator. fMRI+MEG localise it to posterior insula / ventromedial thalamus (proprioceptive-interoceptive, not aversive-mood circuitry). High mapping_fidelity to the proposed REE primitive because the model IS the proposed primitive; transfer_risk low because it is already an abstract control-theoretic accumulator, not a species-specific circuit.
failure_signatures: If REE registered fatigue as a single-threshold flag rather than a two-bound hysteretic accumulator, it would lose the 'recover' half (no lower bound to gate re-engagement) and could chatter at the stop threshold -- the model shows stop AND resume are distinct bound-crossings.
Incentive does not abolish the accumulator; it rescales slopes/bounds (lets the agent 'work closer to exhaustion'). A model where high reward simply switches fatigue off would contradict the data.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Decisions to cease and resume work are triggered by a cost-evidence accumulation signal reaching upper and lower bounds, respectively. The signal accumulates (slope Se) during effort and dissipates (slope Sr) during rest; the gap between bounds is amplitude A. Task difficulty selectively increases Se (shorter work bouts); monetary incentive slows Se, speeds Sr, and widens A (work closer to exhaustion). The signal is expressed in posterior insula and ventromedial thalamus -- proprioception/pain-matrix regions, not reward or aversive-mood circuitry.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the recommended smallest computational form for a fatigue/stop-recover control signal on the SD-012 homeostatic side: a scalar F with F += Se*effort during exertion and F -= Sr during rest; F >= F_upper emits stop/disengage; F is allowed to recover until F <= F_lower before re-engagement. Drive (SD-012 drive_level) and incentive-token strength can modulate the slopes/bounds. The two-bound hysteresis maps structurally onto MECH-342's graded drift-to-a-release-bound, so fatigue can feed the MECH-342 commit-maintenance-release accumulator as a new deficit input while keeping a distinct SIGNAL.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human button-press squeeze-force task over minutes; the accumulator is a phenomenological fit, not a metabolic measurement. REE's 'effort' is not yet operationalised (action cost? compute? plan depth?), so Se must be defined before the model can be instantiated. The model captures the WITHIN-task break decision; the longer-horizon sleep-pressure variant (Process S, Borbely 2016 in this directory) is a slower second accumulator, not the same variable.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults; physical effort (handgrip) and an analogous cognitive task; behavioural model fit + fMRI + MEG.

confidence_components.notes: PNAS, converging fMRI+MEG, formal model with identifiable parameters. Mapping_fidelity high because the paper's model is essentially the proposed REE primitive in control-theoretic form. Transfer_risk low: the object is already a domain-general accumulator; the main open question is REE's definition of per-step effort, not species transfer.
